sentences.zh: 与此同时，他也在为自己不被世界理解而悲伤。

sentences.en: So he's retreating inward, but also grieving and sad that he is not understood by more people or can't bring his internal vision out in a way.
sentences.zh: 所以他向内退隐，但也因为不被更多人理解，或者无法以某种方式表达他的内在愿景而感到悲伤和难过。

sentences.en: And him spending time in that internal vision of the top of the tower helps him clarify it and rarify it and process it so that he can bring out a revelation to people so that not just he can have the experience internal,
sentences.zh: 他在塔顶沉浸于那种内在愿景，帮助他澄清、升华并处理它，这样他就能给人们带来启示，不仅是他自己能有这种内在体验，

sentences.en: but a lot of the Jungian ethics, his personal ethics was that you can retreat into the unconscious, you can retreat into the self,
sentences.zh: 而且许多荣格的伦理，他个人的伦理是，你可以退隐到无意识中，你可以退隐到自我中，

sentences.en: but you need to bring something back for other people.
sentences.zh: 但你需要为其他人带回一些东西。

sentences.en: You need to bring something back that is not just for you, but for everyone.
sentences.zh: 你需要带回一些不仅是为了你自己，而是为了每个人的东西。

sentences.en: And I think one of the biggest arguments in that book is that what he brings out of it is that it's not just that we have the obligation to go past the unlived life of the parent and to go past,
sentences.zh: 我认为那本书中最大的论点之一是，他从中带出来的是，我们不仅有义务超越父母未竟的生活，超越……

sentences.en: you know, where our parents didn't quite finish their lives themselves, but we have the responsibility to go past the unlived life of all of the dead in human culture.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们父母自己没有完全过完的生活，我们还有责任超越人类文化中所有死者未竟的生活。

sentences.en: All the things that humanity has not dealt with, all the things that humanity has not done yet, and that we need to find a way to transcend, you know, our animal nature.
sentences.zh: 人类尚未处理的所有事情，人类尚未完成的所有事情，我们需要找到一种方式来超越，你知道，我们的动物本性。

sentences.en: We need to find a way to transcend our bias and our, not just personal shadow, but our cultural and human shadow.
sentences.zh: 我们需要找到一种方式来超越我们的偏见，不仅是个人阴影，还有我们的文化和人类阴影。

sentences.en: And that's kind of their argument, I think, in Moment for the Dead is that that's what he is saying with the Red Book.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是他们在《为死者哀悼》中的论点，这就是他在《红书》（Red Book）中所说的。

sentences.en: And a lot of that is made while he's contemplating the murals in that tower and painting them.
sentences.zh: 其中很多是在他沉思塔里的壁画并绘制它们时完成的。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, that's very well put, Joel.
sentences.zh: 是啊，不，说得太好了，乔尔。

sentences.en: I think that the, in fact, Shantasani argues that really that the tower, and I agree with him, the tower is a continuation of the Red Book.
sentences.zh: 我认为，事实上，沙达尼认为，我也同意他，这座塔是《红书》的延续。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You know, it's a three-dimensional.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它是三维的。

sentences.en: And the tower, the Red Book is brought out of the tower in a certain way.
sentences.zh: 而且《红书》在某种程度上是从塔中带出来的。

sentences.en: Even if he's not working on it there, he's spending the formative time in the self there and then bringing it out.
sentences.zh: 即使他不在那里创作它，他也在那里度过沉淀自我的时间，然后把它带出来。

sentences.en: That's the relic, you know?
sentences.zh: 那是遗物，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, actually, if you look at quite a lot of the pictures in the Red Book, I mean, particularly the Mandala one of the fort, he's, well, there's actually one,
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上，如果你看《红书》中的很多图片，我的意思是，特别是那个堡垒的曼陀罗，他，嗯，实际上有一张，

sentences.en: I can't remember the chapter, I think it's chapter two.
sentences.zh: 我不记得是哪一章了，我想是第二章。

sentences.en: There's an element called The Castle by the Lake, which actually, I think the date of that is 1913, is pretty well a vision of the tower as in, you know, like, you know, 20, 30,
sentences.zh: 有一个元素叫“湖畔城堡”，实际上，我认为它的日期是1913年，这几乎就是塔的愿景，就像，你知道，20、30、

sentences.en: 40 years later.
sentences.zh: 40年后那样。

sentences.en: So, I think it's a kind of ongoing, you know, it almost transcends time, that there's this kind of slippage between the imagery of the Red Book and the tower itself.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这是一种持续的，你知道，它几乎超越了时间，在《红书》的意象和塔本身之间存在着这种滑移。

sentences.en: So, I was going to say something else, and it's just gone out of my mind.
sentences.zh: 所以，我本来想说点别的，但它刚从我脑子里溜走了。

sentences.en: Yeah, oh, no, the, you know, it's, I mean, really, what's called the spiritual tower, which is the, let's call it the third phase, 1931.
sentences.zh: 是啊，哦，不，你知道，它是，我的意思是，真的，所谓的“精神之塔”，也就是，我们称之为第三阶段，1931年。

sentences.en: And, I think, has quite a lot of link to Ravenna, his trip to Ravenna.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为这与拉文纳，也就是他去拉文纳的旅行，有着相当多的联系。

sentences.en: But, I think that is his inward place, you know, the most connected timber place.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得那是他的内心之地，你知道，最能让他产生共鸣的木质空间。

sentences.en: The fifth episode, at the top, is much more transparent, and it has a timber frame, so it's kind of open to the lake.
sentences.zh: 第五个房间，也就是顶层，要通透得多，而且它有木框架，所以它算是向湖面敞开的。

sentences.en: So, you've got this kind of delicious, it's not really a dualism, because it sort of transcends it, you know, there's this kind of closed openness.
sentences.zh: 所以，你拥有这种美妙的——这其实算不上二元论，因为它在某种程度上超越了二元论，你知道，这是一种封闭的开放性。

sentences.en: In equal measure.
sentences.zh: 两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: I mean, as you said earlier on, I think his disenchantment with the world,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如你刚才所说，我认为他对这个世界的幻灭感，

sentences.en: you know, he puts it in terms of, like Merlin, he had to retreat to a tower in the wood, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，他将其比作梅林，他不得不退隐到森林里的塔楼中，你知道，

sentences.en: because the world was too damn stupid.
sentences.zh: 因为这个世界实在太愚蠢了。

sentences.en: I think it is a kind of, well, Gigrich has been very critical of that, that kind of renouncing of the world, you know, he calls it a sort of psycho Disneyland,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种——嗯，吉格里奇对这种放弃世界的行为非常批判，你知道，他称之为一种“心理迪士尼乐园”，

sentences.en: which is pretty harsh, I think.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这评价相当刻薄。

sentences.en: And he's not alone, you know, people like Rilke, Raina Maria Rilke, or the Irish poet Yeats, they all retreat to powers.
sentences.zh: 而且他并不孤单，你知道，像里尔克、赖内·马利亚·里尔克，或者爱尔兰诗人叶芝，他们都退隐到了塔楼中。

sentences.en: So, there is a kind of post-war pattern.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种战后的模式。

sentences.en: Well, and I think, too, Jung, one of the things David Tacey pointed out on our last interview was that, like, Jung borrows a lot of ideas from Hinduism.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我认为，荣格也是如此。大卫·泰西在我们上次采访中指出的事情之一就是，荣格借鉴了很多印度教的思想。

sentences.en: And one of the images is that relationship between Brahman and Atman, that the self and God have a relationship and are through religion merged together.
sentences.zh: 其中一个意象是梵与我的关系，即自我与神之间存在一种关系，并通过宗教融合在一起。

sentences.en: But, or ritual or whatever, you know, whatever you want to call it, liminal space.
sentences.zh: 但是，或者说仪式，或者无论你怎么称呼它，那种阈限空间。

sentences.en: But I think another one that doesn't get as much, it's not talked about as much that he takes from Hinduism is that there's the idea of Dharma and Moksha in Hinduism,
sentences.zh: 但我认为他从印度教中借鉴的另一个不太被提及、讨论得也不够多的概念是“达摩”和“莫克沙”，

sentences.en: that you have to have a world renunciation, giving up your belongings, wandering and retreating from the world into the woods.
sentences.zh: 即你必须放弃世界，舍弃财产，流浪并从世俗退隐到森林中。

sentences.en: That is part of spirituality, but so is the world sustaining, having children, raising a family, giving to the poor, contributing to society, using your intellect.
sentences.zh: 那是灵性的一部分，但维持世俗生活——生儿育女、养家糊口、救济穷人、贡献社会、运用智慧——同样也是。

sentences.en: That also is the way that is a responsibility of the religious person.
sentences.zh: 这也是宗教人士的责任所在。

sentences.en: So, the relationship between those, and in the Hindu tradition, there's a lot of, some people say, well, you do this at the beginning of your life, and at the end,
sentences.zh: 所以，这两者之间的关系，在印度教传统中，很多人说，嗯，你在人生的开始和结束时做这件事，

sentences.en: you go into the woods.
sentences.zh: 你走进森林。

sentences.en: Or, well, you do this, and then you take the realization, and you bring it back into life.
sentences.zh: 或者，嗯，你先经历这些，然后获得觉悟，再将其带回生活中。

sentences.en: And, you know, they try and, because these are opposites, but the tension of those opposites is something that is interesting to Jung.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们试图——因为这些是对立的，但这种对立的张力是荣格感兴趣的东西。

sentences.en: And I kind of see some of that in Bollinger, that he's retreating into himself at the same time that he's trying to formulate something to bring out of himself.
sentences.zh: 我在博林根也看到了这一点，他在退隐到自我的同时，也在试图构思出某种东西，以便从自我中带出来。

sentences.en: I don't know if that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 不知道这是否说得通。

sentences.en: No, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 不，完全说得通。

sentences.en: I think there's two things that come to mind when you talk about that.
sentences.zh: 当你谈到这一点时，我想到了两件事。

sentences.en: The first, it inverts the story.
sentences.zh: 首先，它颠倒了这个故事。

sentences.en: It becomes a businessman, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 它变成了一个商人的故事，不是吗？

sentences.en: And then returns, you know, that story.
sentences.zh: 然后又回归了，你知道，就是那个故事。

sentences.en: But more potently, I think Bruder Klaus, the Swiss mystic, who Mark Twain was quite playful about, because he was a saint who had a wife and 10 kids.
sentences.zh: 但更具影响力的是，我认为是瑞士神秘主义者克劳斯兄弟，马克·吐温曾对他颇为戏谑，因为他是一位有妻子和10个孩子的圣人。

sentences.en: And then when he was 50, he just kind of left home.
sentences.zh: 然后在50岁时，他离家出走了。

sentences.en: So, you know, and actually Jung talks about Bruder Klaus quite a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，实际上荣格经常谈论克劳斯兄弟。

sentences.en: It's that balancing of, you know, in effect, family life and the solitary life.
sentences.zh: 这实际上就是家庭生活与独处生活之间的平衡。

sentences.en: And it's kind of inevitable that it splits, isn't it, in a way, Cushnapton and Bollinger.
sentences.zh: 而且这种分裂在某种程度上是不可避免的，不是吗，库斯纳赫特和博林根。

sentences.en: Well, he's writing a red book in the evenings, you know, while he's seeing patients and spending time with his children and family, which he says is an anchor.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他在晚上写《红书》，你知道，同时还要看病人，花时间陪伴孩子和家人，他说这是他的锚。

sentences.en: His family and his children were an anchor that saved him from psychosis while he was exploring a psychotic episode.
sentences.zh: 他的家人和孩子是他的一根锚，在他探索精神病发作期间，这根锚拯救了他，使他免于陷入精神错乱。

sentences.en: Yeah, I suppose what we should remember, though, that actually, and I don't mean this with any cynicism, that Bollinger is a holiday home.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想我们应该记住，虽然——我并没有任何讽刺的意思——博林根其实是一个度假屋。

sentences.en: And actually, a lot of photographs, you know, the kids are playing.
sentences.zh: 实际上，很多照片里，你知道，孩子们在玩耍。

sentences.en: He's sitting by the lake, you know, playing with the water.
sentences.zh: 他坐在湖边，你知道，玩着水。

sentences.en: So, you know, it isn't this kind of culling of family life.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这并不是那种对家庭生活的摒弃。

sentences.en: It's not a church.
sentences.zh: 它不是一座教堂。

sentences.en: It's not supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 它本就不该是。

sentences.en: It's a retreat for a family.
sentences.zh: 它是家庭的隐居处。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, I suppose that's why he has to find a retreat within a retreat, if you like, which was your point.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我想这就是为什么他必须在隐居处中再找一个隐居处，如果你愿意这么说的话，这正是你的观点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, kind of going up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是往上走。

sentences.en: I mean, I guess, I mean, he used to put up a yellow flag partly for his neighbor to, in effect, repel their children because they would come around and knock.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我猜，他过去常挂起一面黄旗，部分是为了让邻居知道，实际上是想挡住他们的孩子，因为他们会过来敲门。

sentences.en: And the yellow flag meant, you know, no, you know, I'm writing.
sentences.zh: 而黄旗的意思是，你知道，不，你知道，我在写作。

sentences.en: I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's the signals.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是信号。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, the enclosure that includes the loger, really, he describes as, I felt a need for a piece of fenced in land.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道，那个包含小木屋的围栏，他描述说，我感到需要一块有围栏的土地。

sentences.en: But really, he probably got fed up with people like me coming along the lake saying, oh, there's Carl Jung and his wife.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他可能只是厌倦了像我这样沿着湖边走过来的人说：“哦，那是卡尔·荣格和他的妻子。”

sentences.en: And he spent time in Bollington with Einstein, too, drinking red wine and talking about physics and ultimately coming up with the theory of synchronicity, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且他在博林根也和爱因斯坦待过，喝着红酒，谈论物理学，最终提出了共时性理论，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, it was Einstein's Pauli, wasn't it, I think?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是爱因斯坦的泡利，不是吗，我想？

sentences.en: Wolfgang Pauli.
sentences.zh: 沃尔夫冈·泡利。

sentences.en: I thought Einstein was.
sentences.zh: 我以为是爱因斯坦。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I know Pauli and Einstein.
sentences.zh: 我知道泡利和爱因斯坦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I didn't mean to.
sentences.zh: 所以我不是故意的。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不确定。

sentences.en: But I don't know what kind of wine Pauli liked it.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道泡利喜欢喝什么样的酒。

sentences.en: I know him and Jung and Einstein shared a passion for red.
sentences.zh: 我知道他和荣格以及爱因斯坦都对红酒情有独钟。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I think Wolfgang Pauli, because he has a really interesting double character.
sentences.zh: 是的，嗯，我认为沃尔夫冈·泡利，因为他有一个非常有趣的双重性格。

sentences.en: I think he probably liked any wine, I should think.
sentences.zh: 我想他可能什么酒都喜欢，我猜。

sentences.en: But, you know, the loger that's used, you know, I think we could call it a spiritual place or a sacred place.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，所使用的小木屋，你知道，我认为我们可以称之为精神之地或神圣之地。

sentences.en: And his encounters with Victor White and, you know, the controversy and the construction of Answer to Job have a lot to do with the tower.
sentences.zh: 他与维克多·怀特的相遇，以及你知道的争议，还有《答约伯》的创作，都与这座塔楼有很大关系。

sentences.en: And rather sadly, when they kind of fall out, when they meet after that, Jung only invites Victor White to Kushnacht.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，当他们闹翻后，在那之后他们见面时，荣格只邀请维克多·怀特去库斯纳赫特。

sentences.en: He doesn't, you know, he's kind of lost his rights, if you like.
sentences.zh: 他没有，你知道，他算是失去了他的权利，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: So in a sense, the tower is slightly politicized in a logical sense.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，这座塔在逻辑意义上被稍微政治化了。

sentences.en: But, yeah, you know, I mean, another interesting thing to think about is the way that it becomes a tower, because it's not a tower.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，你知道，我的意思是，另一个值得思考的有趣之处在于它变成塔楼的方式，因为它并不是一座塔。

sentences.en: Not a tower.
sentences.zh: 不是一座塔。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And if you go back through the letters, early on, he talks about is my country seat, my little place in the country.
sentences.zh: 如果你翻看书信，早些时候，他谈到的是“我的乡间别墅，我在乡下的小地方”。

sentences.en: And then a few years later, it becomes the tower, my tower with a little T.
sentences.zh: 然后几年后，它变成了“塔楼”，我的小写t的塔楼。

sentences.en: And then it becomes the tower.
sentences.zh: 然后它变成了“塔楼”。

sentences.en: So it's an internal space that's being brought up there.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个被带到那里的内在空间。

sentences.en: It's not as much of a physical change.
sentences.zh: 这并不是物理上的巨大改变。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, he does build a tower, but when you see it, you see a house.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他确实盖了一座塔，但当你看到它时，你看到的是一所房子。

sentences.en: You don't really, it doesn't look, register as a tower.
sentences.zh: 你真的不会，它看起来不像，也不会被认为是一座塔。

sentences.en: Yeah, true.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, there are tower-like elements.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，确实有类似塔的元素。

sentences.en: I mean, they say the spiritual tower is, you know, it's quite slender and elongated.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们说精神之塔是，你知道，它相当细长。

sentences.en: But the first tower is quite stumpy.
sentences.zh: 但第一座塔相当粗短。

sentences.en: But it doesn't matter, because, but what I find interesting is that it starts to breed its own symbol, if you like.
sentences.zh: 但这没关系，因为，但我发现有趣的是，它开始孕育出它自己的象征，如果你愿意的话。

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, he would declare in MDR that, you know, he wanted to sort of constellate or concrete his ideas in form.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他在《回忆、梦、思考》中宣称，你知道，他想以某种形式来构思或具体化他的思想。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's this kind of logical move to architecture.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是一种通向建筑的逻辑举动。

sentences.en: I think that's kind of true in a way.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在某种程度上是正确的。

sentences.en: But I think it, it's sort of a narrative that's slightly constructed.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它，这是一种稍微构建出来的叙事。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't mean any disrespect to you, but, you know, I love the man.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我无意冒犯你，但是，你知道，我热爱这个人。

sentences.en: But I think it, it's an ordinary place that becomes extraordinary, you know, rather than it is an extraordinary place.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它，它是一个变得非凡的普通地方，你知道，而不是它本身就是一个非凡的地方。

sentences.en: But, you know, you can't.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，你不能。

sentences.en: That's an interesting perspective.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的视角。

sentences.en: I mean, so I guess there are, like, two questions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所以我猜有两个问题。

sentences.en: One, you know, what, do you have any idea or any speculation what is in the tower?
sentences.zh: 第一，你知道，什么，你有什么想法或推测塔里有什么吗？

sentences.en: You know, what's up there that no one has seen?
sentences.zh: 你知道，上面有什么是没人见过的？

sentences.en: And two, you know, Carl Jung's a guy who sees all these patterns in life, religion, self, and starts to inventory them.
sentences.zh: 第二，你知道，卡尔·荣格是一个在生活、宗教、自我中看到所有这些模式，并开始对它们进行编目的人。

sentences.en: You know, do you see patterns in Bollingen and have a sense of what he's doing?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你在博林根看到了什么模式，并对他在做什么有什么感觉吗？

sentences.en: Is there quaternity symbolism or some kind of symbolic element that you feel like you've noticed that no one has seen yet?
sentences.zh: 有没有四元性象征或某种你觉得你已经注意到但还没人发现的象征性元素？

sentences.en: I'm not sure if I'm the only person to notice it, but I think I'm just going to read something, actually, which I've got on the screen, which might help.
sentences.zh: 我不确定我是唯一注意到它的人，但我认为我打算读一些东西，实际上，我屏幕上有这些内容，可能会有帮助。

sentences.en: This is a letter to a guy called Peter de Brandt, written in 1959.
sentences.zh: 这是一封写给一个叫彼得·德·布兰特的人的信，写于1959年。

sentences.en: And there's a student of architecture who writes to him about sort of archetypal patterns in architecture.
sentences.zh: 有一位建筑系学生写信给他，谈论建筑中的原型模式。

sentences.en: And his response broadly is the circle and the square are connected with the idea of shelter and protection, place of the hearth, concentration, the family and the small animals.
sentences.zh: 他的回答大体上是：圆和方与庇护和保护、炉边、集中、家庭和小动物的概念有关。

sentences.en: And on a higher level, with the symbol of the quateria, I don't know if I pronounce that correctly, as the dwelling place of the inner man, the abode of gods.
sentences.zh: 而在更高的层面上，与四元性的象征——我不知道我发音是否正确——作为内在人的居所，神的住所相关。

sentences.en: So I think in more direct answer to your question, I think the circle and the square oscillate and then sort of constellate into this triangle.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，更直接地回答你的问题，我认为圆和方在振荡，然后构思成这个三角形。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of sort of essay in cycle geometry, but then you get these kind of intermediate spaces that can't be geometrized, if that's a word.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种关于循环几何的论文，但随后你会得到这些无法被几何化的中间空间，如果这算是一个词的话。

sentences.en: So it's kind of geometric and not in equal measure.
sentences.zh: 所以它在某种程度上是几何的，在某种程度上又不是，两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: But you do see the geometry kind of talking to it.
sentences.zh: 但你确实看到了几何形状在与它对话。

sentences.en: You see his visual thought process there.
sentences.zh: 你在那里看到了他的视觉思维过程。

sentences.en: That's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 那太迷人了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, the role of Franz Jung, his son, is very underestimated.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道，他的儿子弗朗茨·荣格的作用被严重低估了。

sentences.en: It's a really lovely book that's just come out, which I'll mention.
sentences.zh: 有一本非常可爱的书刚刚出版，我会提到它。

sentences.en: I can't find it.
sentences.zh: 我找不到它。

sentences.en: But anyway, it's it's called About France and it's by an American woman.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，它叫《关于弗朗茨》，是一位美国女性写的。

sentences.en: So you should be able to get it in your country that talks about her visit or part of it talks about her visit to the tower with Franz Jung,
sentences.zh: 所以你应该能在你们国家买到，它谈到了她的访问，或者其中一部分谈到了她与弗朗茨·荣格对塔楼的访问，

sentences.en: who probably was involved with almost all of it.
sentences.zh: 他可能参与了几乎所有的建造工作。

sentences.en: And so he could unpack some of the kind of narrative and some of the complexity of of complicated geometry is sort of crashing into each other.
sentences.zh: 所以他可以解开一些叙事，以及一些复杂的几何形状相互碰撞的复杂性。

sentences.en: So I think in answer to your question, I think there's the circle and the square.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，回答你的问题，我认为有圆和方。

sentences.en: Very evident.
sentences.zh: 非常明显。

sentences.en: And we can trace that back to the painting that he looks at in the rectory in Klein Hunnigan.
sentences.zh: 我们可以追溯到他在克莱因·亨宁根的牧师住宅里看到的那幅画。

sentences.en: It's a painting called the David with the head of Goliath by Guido Reni, which has David leaning on a circular column with the head of Goliath on a square column.
sentences.zh: 那是一幅圭多·雷尼画的《大卫与歌利亚的头》，画中大卫靠在一根圆柱上，歌利亚的头放在一根方柱上。

sentences.en: And he's absolutely transfixed by this in the dark, in the dark, sequestered room.
sentences.zh: 他在黑暗、幽静的房间里被这幅画深深吸引。

sentences.en: And I think in his youth.
sentences.zh: 我想是在他年轻的时候。

sentences.en: Attics, towers, chapels, squares, circles.
sentences.zh: 阁楼、塔楼、礼拜堂、正方形、圆形。

sentences.en: Gather, you know, in a way, I'm probably seeing that into it, but I think they gather around castles.
sentences.zh: 聚集，你知道，在某种程度上，我可能是在过度解读，但我认为它们聚集在城堡周围。

sentences.en: He draws castles.
sentences.zh: 他画城堡。

sentences.en: The architecture in the Red Book has a lot of, you know, circle above a town, above a tower, above, you know, things.
sentences.zh: 《红书》里的建筑有很多，你知道，城镇上方的圆，塔楼上方的圆，你知道，各种东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the the the fort that is drawn in the Red Book actually is a fort that pretty well existed during Jung's time.
sentences.zh: 而且《红书》中画的那座堡垒，实际上是一座在荣格时代确实存在的堡垒。

sentences.en: It was destroyed with the by the in the Treaty of Paris.
sentences.zh: 它在《巴黎条约》中被摧毁了。

sentences.en: But it's ramparts existed.
sentences.zh: 但它的城墙依然存在。

sentences.en: And it's not not an exact.
sentences.zh: 它不是完全准确的。

sentences.en: It's not exactly like the picture in the Red Book, but he reconstructs it in his mind as this kind of star fort.
sentences.zh: 它不完全像《红书》里的那张图，但他把它在脑海中重构为这种星形要塞。

sentences.en: So I think he's looking.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他在寻找。

sentences.en: He's looking.
sentences.zh: 他在寻找。

sentences.en: You might say unconsciously in his formative years and consciously when he goes to the stupas of India and the the council house,
sentences.zh: 你可能会说，在他成长的岁月里是无意识的，而当他去印度的佛塔和议会大厦时，是有意识的，

sentences.en: the council to call to the council building in Fatima Sipri in India.
sentences.zh: 在印度法塔赫布尔西格里的议会大厦。

sentences.en: He's he's he's searching out sacred geometry, but in his youth, it's more.
sentences.zh: 他一直在寻找神圣几何，但在他年轻时，它更多是。

sentences.en: It's sort of it's not so much in the background, but it's more unconscious, I suppose you would say.
sentences.zh: 它与其说是在背景中，不如说更多是无意识的，我想你会这么说。

sentences.en: Well, can you clarify sacred geometry just a little bit for people who may not be as aware of Western esoteria?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你能为那些可能不太了解西方神秘学的人稍微澄清一下“神圣几何”吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, quickly put, I think that, you know, if we go back to that, that quote from Jung to the to the student, that the essence essence, I suppose, is contained.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，简单来说，我觉得，你知道，如果我们回到那个荣格对学生说的话，那种本质，我想，是包含在里面的。

sentences.en: The essence of man and the essence of God is a kind of mystical union is contained in pure geometry.
sentences.zh: 人的本质和上帝的本质，是一种神秘的结合，包含在纯粹的几何学中。

sentences.en: You know, it's a kind of absolute is almost platonic, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一种绝对，几乎是柏拉图式的，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's a kind of absolute.
sentences.zh: 这是一种绝对。

sentences.en: So, you know, there are different permutations of that, because then you go into sort of polygons and hexagons.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这有不同的排列组合，因为你会进入多边形和六边形之类的领域。

sentences.en: I mean, for example, the most baptisteries are octagonal, the eight, you know, seven plus one, you know, the rebirth.
sentences.zh: 我是说，例如，大多数洗礼堂都是八角形的，八，你知道，七加一，你知道，重生。

sentences.en: And I believe, well, Hannah, Barbara Hannah says that the spiritual tower, you know, which you can't go into, it has eight facets inside.
sentences.zh: 而且我相信，嗯，芭芭拉·汉娜（Barbara Hannah）说那座精神之塔，你知道，你无法进入的那座，里面有八个面。

sentences.en: I don't think it's octagonal, but I think it has eight facets.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它是八角形的，但我认为它有八个面。

sentences.en: So, you know, that's a deliberate move.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是一个刻意的举动。

sentences.en: The font when you go into the tower where he pumps water is eight sided.
sentences.zh: 当你进入他抽水的塔楼时，那个洗礼盆是八边的。

sentences.en: So, you know, I mean, there's these these kind of you see him playing with space and geometry to convey meaning and math to a certain extent to convey meaning.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我是说，有这些，你看到他在玩弄空间和几何来传达意义，在某种程度上用数学来传达意义。

sentences.en: Yeah, I do.
sentences.zh: 是的，我同意。

sentences.en: And then every so often, either his way or, you know, the kind of inverse is sort of endodromeic, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 然后每隔一段时间，无论是他的方式，还是，你知道，那种反向的，有点像内向性的，不是吗？

sentences.en: You know, the inverse of the kind of awkward kind of asymmetric things have to adjust to the next sort of chapter of the geometry.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那种笨拙的、不对称事物的反面，必须调整到几何学的下一个篇章。

sentences.en: So it's a really complex and non-dualistic array, really, which I find fascinating.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是一个非常复杂且非二元论的阵列，我发现这很迷人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And so any idea what's at the top of the tower, what the private rooms in Bollinger are?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于塔顶有什么，博林根（Bollingen）的私人房间是什么，你有什么想法吗？

sentences.en: Do you have any speculation or heard any rumors?
sentences.zh: 你有什么推测或听到过什么传闻吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think I found one picture of the fifth episode, which interestingly is a kind of a concession to habitability because it's got, I believe, a coal fire.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我找到了一张第五集的照片，有趣的是，这算是对宜居性的一种妥协，因为它有，我相信，一个煤火炉。

sentences.en: And so they used to hoist up coal because, you know, Jung was, you know, 80, you know, around that time.
sentences.zh: 所以他们过去常把煤吊上去，因为，你知道，荣格当时，你知道，80岁左右。

sentences.en: So, you know, it wasn't really viable to move wood or to heat up.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，搬运木头或取暖并不太现实。

sentences.en: And the picture looks as though it's certainly in part lined with timber and very much looks out over the lake.
sentences.zh: 照片看起来确实部分衬有木材，而且非常能俯瞰湖泊。

sentences.en: And I find it quite moving because he talks about the other Bollinger, i.e. after death.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很感人，因为他谈到了另一个博林根，即死后。

sentences.en: And this kind of aspect to the beyond.
sentences.zh: 以及这种通往彼岸的层面。

sentences.en: It was a liminal space for him.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，这是一个阈限空间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: It was a transition between, in effect, life and death.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这是生与死之间的一个过渡。

sentences.en: And one biographer, I've forgotten his name, remembers seeing Jung sat in the spiritual tower, which is the next floor down on the second floor.
sentences.zh: 有一位传记作者，我忘了他的名字，记得看到荣格坐在精神之塔里，也就是下一层的二楼。

sentences.en: Absolutely absorbed in his work, you know, in this other world.
sentences.zh: 完全沉浸在他的工作中，你知道，在这个另一个世界里。

sentences.en: So it's kind of a gateway to the tower.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是通往塔楼的门户。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: And then, you know, he talks about the mountains and the majesty of the lake that, you know, as you say, he wants to live by water and the majesty of the mountains and the beyond.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，他谈到了山脉和湖泊的壮丽，正如你所说，他想住在水边，还有山脉和彼岸的壮丽。

sentences.en: Which, ironically, is where the stone came from for the tower.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，塔楼的石头就是从那里来的。

sentences.en: You know, the quarry is on the other side of the lake or one of the mountains.
sentences.zh: 你知道，采石场在湖的另一边，或者在其中一座山上。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it's evocative and in a sense, the closure of the first tower and the super closure of the third tower.
sentences.zh: 所以这很能唤起联想，在某种意义上，是第一座塔的闭合和第三座塔的超级闭合。

sentences.en: Open and, you know, it's a kind of diastole, isn't it, really?
sentences.zh: 开放，你知道，这是一种舒张，不是吗，真的？

sentences.en: If they open and close with these other elements.
sentences.zh: 如果它们随着这些其他元素打开和关闭的话。

sentences.en: And it's hard sometimes to fit all the elements of architecture into a conversation, but you see the space kind of having a conversation,
sentences.zh: 有时很难将建筑的所有元素融入对话中，但你看到空间在进行某种对话，

sentences.en: but it's hard to articulate it because it's a visual language.
sentences.zh: 但很难表达出来，因为它是一种视觉语言。

sentences.en: It's not a cognitive, you know, language, a word based language.
sentences.zh: 它不是一种认知的，你知道，语言，一种基于文字的语言。

sentences.en: But it sounds like you have a real sense of what he's doing there and how he saw it, you know, after spending the time you've spent there.
sentences.zh: 但听起来你对他所做的事情以及他如何看待它有很深的理解，你知道，在你花时间待在那里之后。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, I suppose the other thing we can draw into our conversation is the house dream in 1909, when he's coming back with Freud from America.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我们可以引入对话的另一件事是1909年的房子梦，当时他正和弗洛伊德从美国回来。

sentences.en: You know, I think a lot of the tower, I don't think the tower is a replica of the dream, but it has elements of the dream in it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为塔楼的很多部分，我不认为塔楼是梦境的复制品，但它里面有梦境的元素。

sentences.en: And I think what's interesting about that is that it's kind of palimpsest structure, you know, that one thing lying on top of another.
sentences.zh: 我认为有趣的是，它是一种重写本结构，你知道，一层覆盖着另一层。

sentences.en: When he discovers the body of the soldier, it gives the cellar, prior to that, I mean, it's not literally a cellar, but, you know, it's got this kind of subterranean space,
sentences.zh: 当他发现士兵的尸体时，它给了地窖，在此之前，我是说，它不是字面意义上的地窖，但，你知道，它有这种地下空间，

sentences.en: if you think of the dream.
sentences.zh: 如果你想到那个梦的话。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think the,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为，

sentences.en: well, I've written a whole chapter on that, the relationship of the dream as a kind of guide, if you like, to the tower without it being a, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我写了整整一章关于这个，梦作为一种指南的关系，如果你愿意的话，通向塔楼，而不是说，你知道，

sentences.en: the building is a dream, you know.
sentences.zh: 建筑本身就是一个梦，你知道。

sentences.en: So that's another aspect.
sentences.zh: 所以这是另一个方面。

sentences.en: Well, is there anything that we don't get to that you feel like is important about knowledge?
sentences.zh: 嗯，关于知识，有什么我们没谈到但你觉得很重要的吗？

sentences.en: Jim, those are kind of the questions that I had.
sentences.zh: 吉姆，这些就是我有的问题。

sentences.en: I don't know a ton about it, other than just what comes up in Memories, Dreams, Reflections, and other people's writing about you.
sentences.zh: 除了在《回忆、梦、思考》以及其他人关于你的著作中提到的内容外，我对此了解不多。

sentences.en: Anything that you feel like is important we haven't hit on?
sentences.zh: 有什么你觉得重要但我们还没谈到的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, I think what is important is to, this isn't the best answer, but I'll start with it, is to trace it deeper into his psychic and physical history.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为重要的是，这不是最好的答案，但我会从这里开始，就是把它追溯到他更深层的心理和身体历史中。

sentences.en: I think Bollinger's configured as this kind of last chapter, if you like, of his work.
sentences.zh: 我认为博林根被配置为他作品的最后一个篇章，如果你愿意的话。

sentences.en: I think it's much more, almost circumlandically, you know, that it's this kind of...
sentences.zh: 我认为它更多是，几乎是环绕式的，你知道，它是这种……

sentences.en: It grows as he grows.
sentences.zh: 它随着他的成长而成长。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And I think, I have a sense, I've not been entirely been able to constellate this, is that he, in a sense, the building is designing itself.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，我有一种感觉，我还没能完全理清，就是他，在某种意义上，建筑本身在自我设计。

sentences.en: It has a kind of architectural unconscious, if you like.
sentences.zh: 它有一种建筑上的潜意识，如果你愿意的话。

sentences.en: He was listening to the place and then helping it be birthed.
sentences.zh: 他在倾听这个地方，然后帮助它诞生。

sentences.en: It wasn't his blueprint that he was just building.
sentences.zh: 那不是他只是在建造的蓝图。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: And he talks about that, because when he writes to Christina Morgan, who also built a tower in Americain, he says, well, actually, when you start your building,
sentences.zh: 他谈到了这一点，因为当他写信给克里斯蒂娜·摩根（Christina Morgan）时，她也在美国建了一座塔，他说，嗯，实际上，当你开始建造时，

sentences.en: you'll know that it releases all sorts of spirits.
sentences.zh: 你会知道它释放了各种各样的灵魂。

sentences.en: He doesn't call them spirits, but ghoulies or something like that, you know.
sentences.zh: 他不称它们为灵魂，而是小妖精之类的东西，你知道。

sentences.en: So there was this literally genius...
sentences.zh: 所以这里确实有一种天才……

sentences.en: Spectres, maybe, is that the word?
sentences.zh: 幽灵，也许，是这个词吗？

sentences.en: Pardon?
sentences.zh: 抱歉？

sentences.en: Spectre, is that the word?
sentences.zh: 幽灵，是这个词吗？

sentences.en: No, anyway, you know, we get to the art, you know, and so I think he's listening, which is an architectural act, but I think it's much more, it's much richer than that.
sentences.zh: 不，总之，你知道，我们谈到了艺术，你知道，所以我认为他在倾听，这是一种建筑行为，但我认为它远不止于此，它丰富得多。

sentences.en: I think the art, the building is leading his ideas, responding to his ideas.
sentences.zh: 我认为艺术，建筑在引导他的思想，响应他的思想。

sentences.en: You know, if you look at his diagrams, as you trace them through the collective works, they become much more three-dimensional.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你看他的图表，当你追踪它们穿过全集时，它们变得更加三维了。

sentences.en: So I think there's this kind of traffic...
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这里有一种交通……

sentences.en: He's paying religious attention to the space and the building.
sentences.zh: 他以宗教般的虔诚关注着空间和建筑。

sentences.en: Absolutely, yeah.
sentences.zh: 绝对是，是的。

sentences.en: And then a second point is the kind of legacy of the tower.
sentences.zh: 第二点是塔楼的遗产。

sentences.en: So Marie van France built a tower, well, it was designed by Franz Jung's son.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·冯·弗朗茨（Marie-Louise von Franz）建了一座塔，嗯，是由弗朗茨·荣格（Franz Jung）的儿子设计的。

sentences.en: And I'm very grateful to Gotti, who lives there, who shared with me the drawings, which are beautiful drawings of this tower.
sentences.zh: 我非常感谢住在那里并与我分享图纸的戈蒂（Gotti），那些是这座塔的美丽图纸。

sentences.en: So her tower becomes the kind of perfect tower, in inverted commas, because it's this quadrate.
sentences.zh: 所以她的塔成了所谓的完美塔，加了引号，因为它是这个四方形。

sentences.en: You know, it doesn't have to evolve, it's just this fixed thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它不需要进化，它只是这个固定的东西。

sentences.en: And Christina Morgan's tower is this very slender, circular thing.
sentences.zh: 而克里斯蒂娜·摩根的塔是一个非常细长的圆形东西。

sentences.en: So the circle and the square come back, you know, in this kind of legacy.
sentences.zh: 所以圆和方又回来了，你知道，在这种遗产中。

sentences.en: I mean, I just think they're all fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我只是觉得它们都很迷人。

sentences.en: And I suppose, you know, I think Marie van France got a bit fed up with Jung saying, well, you know, your tower needs to be like this, it's my tower, you know.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，我认为玛丽·冯·弗朗茨对荣格说“嗯，你知道，你的塔需要像这样，这是我的塔，你知道”有点厌烦了。

sentences.en: Get out of it, sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 走开之类的话。

sentences.en: But I think that the main point, to answer your lead, is that it's the reciprocity.
sentences.zh: 但我认为主要的一点，回答你的引导，是互惠性。

sentences.en: It's the reciprocity between place, psyche, ideas.
sentences.zh: 这是地方、心灵、思想之间的互惠。

sentences.en: It's a kind of psychic place, you know.
sentences.zh: 这是一种心理场所，你知道。

sentences.en: And I suppose it's not a singular ambition.
sentences.zh: 我想这不是一个单一的野心。

sentences.en: It's about the voice of the natural world, the lake lapping in, those who visit, Tony Wolfe.
sentences.zh: 它是关于自然世界的声音，湖水拍打的声音，那些来访的人，托尼·沃尔夫（Toni Wolff）。

sentences.en: Tony Wolfe's role must have been enormous in the tower.
sentences.zh: 托尼·沃尔夫在塔楼里的角色一定非常巨大。

sentences.en: Franz Jung's, you know, the builders.
sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·荣格的，你知道，那些建筑工人。

sentences.en: You know, so this idea of this kind of solitary figure with this solitary kind of symbol is reductive, I think.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以这种带有这种孤独符号的孤独人物的想法，我认为是还原论的。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, that's a living symbol for sure.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，那肯定是一个活生生的象征。

sentences.en: So any speculation on things that are there that haven't been seen or any rumor?
sentences.zh: 那么对于那里存在但尚未被看到的东西，或者任何传闻，有什么推测吗？

sentences.en: Or do you like the mystery of, you know, it's not ever fully open or known?
sentences.zh: 或者你喜欢这种神秘感，你知道，它从未完全开放或为人所知？

sentences.en: I like the mystery.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这种神秘感。

sentences.en: Initially, I was going to ask the, maybe what, the Jung family, and maybe one day I'll be brave enough to do this, to say, could I measure the whole of this building,
sentences.zh: 最初，我打算问，也许，荣格家族，也许有一天我会足够勇敢去做这件事，去说，我能测量这座建筑的全部吗，

sentences.en: do a drawing of the whole of the building?
sentences.zh: 做一张整个建筑的图纸？

sentences.en: And there'd be like a blueprint of it.
sentences.zh: 然后就会有一张它的蓝图。

sentences.en: I don't think there are blueprints because I think I've tried to track, some of them would have had building, some methods would have had building permits,
sentences.zh: 我不认为有蓝图，因为我想我试着追踪过，其中一些会有建筑，一些方法会有建筑许可，

sentences.en: but there was a fire in the St. Garland Archive.
sentences.zh: 但在圣加仑档案馆发生了一场火灾。

sentences.en: And I, I don't know if they were in there, but I think I have the sense that they don't exist or don't exist now.
sentences.zh: 我，我不知道它们是否在里面，但我认为我有种感觉，它们不存在，或者现在不存在了。

sentences.en: But then more recently, maybe this is post-justified, I just think, in fact, Jung's great-grandson, Daniel, said to me, well, it means different things to different people.
sentences.zh: 但最近，也许这是事后辩解，我只是认为，事实上，荣格的曾孙丹尼尔（Daniel）对我说，嗯，它对不同的人意味着不同的东西。

sentences.en: I think it has to just be universal in its, well, not universal in a way, you know, it's very sort of personal as well as being universal.
sentences.zh: 我认为它必须在它的，嗯，不是以一种普遍的方式，你知道，它非常个人化，同时也具有普遍性。

sentences.en: So I'm kind of fine with the mystery.
sentences.zh: 所以我对这种神秘感没问题。

sentences.en: Well, that's not, that's nice.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那很好。

sentences.en: Well, you know, it's kind of, every time I go, I see something else.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，它有点，每次我去，我都会看到别的东西。

sentences.en: And, you know, obviously, you know, you're just one slightly in conversation with people and you're trying to be polite and respectful and you can't take photographs.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，显然，你知道，你只是在和人交谈，你试图保持礼貌和尊重，你不能拍照。

sentences.en: But out of the sight, if you are, you notice something.
sentences.zh: 但在视线之外，如果你在的话，你会注意到一些东西。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's always giving.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，它总是在给予。

sentences.en: It's always coming alive.
sentences.zh: 它总是活过来的。

sentences.en: And it's still used.
sentences.zh: 而且它还在被使用。

sentences.en: It's not a museum.
sentences.zh: 它不是博物馆。

sentences.en: I mean, it's still used as he intended, almost as is by the family for a holiday.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它仍然像他预期的那样被家人用于度假，几乎原样保留。

sentences.en: Sometimes they're on holiday there and sometimes it's empty.
sentences.zh: 有时他们在那里度假，有时它是空的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that it would be a great shame if it, I think Jung would not be pleased if it became a museum.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为如果它变成博物馆会是一个巨大的遗憾，我想荣格不会高兴的。

sentences.en: You know, obviously that's happened to Freud's Vienna home and actually the London home as well, which is fine.
sentences.zh: 你知道，显然弗洛伊德在维也纳的家，实际上还有伦敦的家也发生了这种情况，这没关系。

sentences.en: So it's not to decry people who've gone down that route.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是要贬低走那条路的人。

sentences.en: But I think, I mean, the way it was explained to me is that it would be difficult to show people around because the stairs are so narrow.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，我是说，向我解释的方式是，带人参观会很困难，因为楼梯太窄了。

sentences.en: But I think that's really a kind of, you know, sort of batting away the problem.
sentences.zh: 但我认为那真的只是一种，你知道，推卸问题的方式。

sentences.en: And this is a home for the Jung family forever, you know, and so should it be, you know.
sentences.zh: 这是荣格家族永远的家，你知道，理应如此，你知道。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, you know, that said, as you've observed, they're very accommodating in, you know, if you knock on the door, you know, which I think is incredible.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，话虽如此，正如你所观察到的，他们非常乐于助人，你知道，如果你敲门的话，你知道，我认为这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: Most of us wouldn't do that, wouldn't we, we'd say.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人不会那样做，不是吗，我们会说。

sentences.en: Especially with the same amount of people who come.
sentences.zh: 特别是考虑到来的人数之多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, I think they try and organize things when people come at the same time.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为当人们同时来时，他们会尝试组织安排。

sentences.en: But, of course, for me, I always wanted just a personal conversation, you know, just, you know, please, please, please, you know, tell me something that will feed my passion,
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，对我来说，我总是只想要一次私人对话，你知道，只是，你知道，请，请，请，你知道，告诉我一些能滋养我热情的东西，

sentences.en: if you like.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话。

sentences.en: Well, is there anything that we can point people to who want to find more about your work or pre-order your book or go to a website?
sentences.zh: 嗯，有什么我们可以指引人们去了解更多关于你的工作，或者预购你的书，或者访问网站的地方吗？

sentences.en: I mean, where can we redirect them, people that are interested in what you've said here?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们可以把他们引向哪里，那些对你在这里所说的话感兴趣的人？

sentences.en: Well, I'd be happy for you to share my email.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我很乐意让你分享我的电子邮件。

sentences.en: Should I read that out?
sentences.zh: 我需要读出来吗？

sentences.en: You can, or I can also put it in the podcast notes, the show notes, if you want that.
sentences.zh: 你可以，或者如果你想要的话，我也可以把它放在播客笔记、节目笔记里。

sentences.en: Yeah, because the moment, I'm hoping that my PhD will be, well, at least written by perhaps January, February, and then I'm really hoping it becomes a book.
sentences.zh: 是啊，因为目前，我希望我的博士论文能在，嗯，至少在1月、2月写完，然后我真的希望它能变成一本书。

sentences.en: So, in answer to a question about a book, that's waiting.
sentences.zh: 所以，回答关于书的问题，那还在等待中。

sentences.en: I do, sometimes lectures I've done have been recorded, and I'd happily do a lecture for someone if, you know, because obviously a lot of this is quite visual.
sentences.zh: 我确实，有时我做过的讲座被录制了下来，如果有人需要，我很乐意为某人做讲座，你知道，因为显然很多东西都很直观。

sentences.en: And so, if we needed to illustrate things more, I could do that.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们需要更多地说明事情，我可以那样做。

sentences.en: But a person that would be, I know that you approached Lucy first, Lucy Huskinson, my supervisor, writes a lot on it.
sentences.zh: 但如果是一个人，我知道你先联系了露西（Lucy），露西·哈斯金森（Lucy Huskinson），我的导师，她写了很多关于这方面的文章。

sentences.en: So, I think that there's...
sentences.zh: 所以，我觉得有……

sentences.en: And Nietzsche is a number of things.
sentences.zh: 尼采有很多面。

sentences.en: Pardon?
sentences.zh: 抱歉？

sentences.en: Nietzsche?
sentences.zh: 尼采？

sentences.en: Like, she does a lot of Nietzsche in architecture also, right?
sentences.zh: 比如，她在建筑学方面也做了很多关于尼采的研究，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，没错。

sentences.en: In fact, she's in the process of finishing a book on that.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她正在完成一本关于此的书。

sentences.en: So, her book, The Architecture of the Mimetic Self, I think is an important, very, very important book.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为她的那本《模仿自我的建筑》是一本非常、非常重要的书。

sentences.en: And obviously, I'm biased, but I do feel that.
sentences.zh: 当然，我可能有偏见，但我确实是这么认为的。

sentences.en: And then Claire Marcus Cooper wrote a really beautiful paper called House Symbolist Self, which is available comparatively easy as a PDF.
sentences.zh: 还有克莱尔·马库斯·库珀写过一篇非常精彩的论文，叫《房屋象征自我》，作为PDF文件很容易就能找到。

sentences.en: So, those...
sentences.zh: 所以，这些……

sentences.en: And then, more recently, Thomas Barry has written about architecture in this sense.
sentences.zh: 最近，托马斯·巴里也从这个角度写过关于建筑的文章。

sentences.en: But in terms of the tower itself, I'm hoping that's my job, because it would put a hole in the side of the ship if someone else was writing.
sentences.zh: 但就这座塔本身而言，我希望那是我的工作，因为如果别人来写，那就像是在船侧面凿了个洞。

sentences.en: But, of course, it would always come from a different perspective and be different.
sentences.zh: 当然，它总是会从不同的角度出发，呈现出不同的样子。

sentences.en: So, I think we have to probably wait, I don't know, six months or something.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想我们可能得等，我不知道，大概六个月左右吧。

sentences.en: So, hopefully, you know, 2023, the book will be for sale.
sentences.zh: 所以，希望在2023年，这本书能上市销售。

sentences.en: So, definitely Google, and I'll share your email address, too, if people want a personalised talk or presentation for an organisation.
sentences.zh: 所以，一定要去谷歌搜索，如果有人需要为某个组织进行个性化的演讲或展示，我也会分享你的电子邮箱地址。

sentences.en: Sorry, Joel, to interrupt.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，乔尔，打断一下。

sentences.en: What would be lovely about 2023 is it would be 100 years after the tower.
sentences.zh: 2023年最美妙的地方在于，那将是这座塔建成100周年。

sentences.en: So, that's my kind of aim.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我的目标。

sentences.en: But it's a glorious obsession that, when I've been dramatic, I've sort of given up everything to do.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种光荣的执念，当我变得戏剧化时，我几乎放弃了一切去追求它。

sentences.en: So, I think the story, or a story, needs to be told about it, which is really why we're talking, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为关于它的故事，或者说其中一个故事，需要被讲述出来，这正是我们今天交谈的原因，不是吗？

sentences.en: But, you know, Martin, your passion is beautiful.
sentences.zh: 但是，马丁，你的热情真的很美。

sentences.en: I really appreciate you sharing that with everybody.
sentences.zh: 我非常感谢你与大家分享这些。

sentences.en: And, you know, I will definitely link to your email address, and then I hope to read your book one day.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我一定会附上你的电子邮箱地址，希望有一天能读到你的书。

sentences.en: So, good luck.
sentences.zh: 祝你好运。

sentences.en: Thank you, Joel, for the opportunity.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，乔尔，给我这个机会。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, what helps is to be able to succinctly summarise what one's doing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然，能够简洁地总结自己正在做的事情是很有帮助的。

sentences.en: So, I want to thank you for the opportunity, and who knows, you know, I think we need, you know, it's an ecological argument, really, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，我想感谢你给我这个机会，谁知道呢，我觉得我们需要，你知道，这其实是一个生态论点，不是吗？

sentences.en: If you really zoomed up, how do we belong to ourselves and to place?
sentences.zh: 如果我们把视角拉大，我们该如何归属于自我和地方？

sentences.en: You know, that's really what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这才是我们真正讨论的内容。

sentences.en: So, thank you.
sentences.zh: 所以，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course, and thank you.
sentences.zh: 好的，当然，也谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for your time.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间。
